key_insight: Training a single model natively on many modalities induces a behavior called Context Unrolling, where the model explicitly iterates and reasons across modality-specific representations before emitting predictions, enabling better integration of complementary signals.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap in multimodal fusion by enabling explicit cross-modal reasoning and aggregation, improving how heterogeneous inputs (text, images, video, 3D, hidden reps) are combined into coherent, shared multimodal knowledge.
method: Native multimodal training: train one unified model on diverse modalities (text, images, video, 3D geometry, latent/hidden representations).
Context Unrolling mechanism: iteratively expose and transform modality-specific representations so the model reasons across them before final decoding.
Cross-modal aggregation: align and fuse complementary information from heterogeneous modalities to approximate a shared multimodal manifold for prediction.
impact: Makes fusion more explicit and interpretable, improving performance and robustness when combining diverse sensory and latent inputs—useful for multimodal search, understanding, and generation in real-world systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing inputs (text, image, video, 3D, hidden reps) feeding into a Context Unrolling block that iteratively exchanges representations before a final prediction head.
Sequence visualization of unrolling steps (time series of intermediate multimodal representations) to illustrate iterative reasoning.
Before/after comparison chart: standard early/late fusion vs. Context Unrolling showing improved alignment and reduced information loss.
Icon set representing each modality (text, image, video, 3D, latent) connected by arrows to emphasize cross-modal aggregation.
paper_authors: Ceyuan Yang, Zhijie Lin, Yang Zhao, Fei Xiao, Hao He
